evidence: Ov. Ars 2.10: longē quem petō portus abest
Cic. Quinct. 79: quam longē est hinc in saltum Gallicānum? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With esse and abesse: longē abest, it’s far; nōn longē, not far; longē ā (ab), far from; further is longius (longius nōn discēdam, I won’t go any further: Cic. Fam. 14.2, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: far off, in the distance, from afar
evidence: Cic. Cat. 2.29: nōn jam procul, sed hīc praesentēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of what is seen, heard or kept far away: procul hinc, keep away! (Mart. 13.25.1).

evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 47: ex locīs tam longinquīs (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: quid properās, juvenis? mediīs tua pīnus in undīs nāvigat, et longē quem petō portus abest
phrases.english: why the hurry, young man? your ship is out in mid-sea, and the harbour I’m making for is far away
Far be it from me to say.
to be a long way off
